John Stow ran a fine opening leg for us coming in 9th (11.21), not too far behind the leaders. We felt that we might now get into the medals with Bill Curtin going on the next leg.

A word of praise for Charlie Walker who is again showing his true form - this enabled him to take first prize in the handicap with John Stow, an up and coming young member second and John Kelly third.

RICHARD CHALLENOR---John Stow and Paddy Breslin are fine prospects who have fared particularly well this season. Paddy won the school 440 in a modest 60.5, but in finishing second in the 880 he recorded a personal best 2:09 repeating John Stow's position of last year.
Open Meeting at Crystal Palace on July 23rd, Peter Carton and John Stow took first two places in the 1500 (Youths) event with 4:08.1 and 4:11.1

Of the remainder, Peter Carton and John Stow set or equalled personal bests but Martin Bloice and Bill Curtin were below their bests, particularly Bill who was last in his heat and seemed very jaded.
Of the six races in which we have competed so far this season we have been placed in all except one (Redhill & Reigate) and in that we were without the services of John Stow and Peter Carton.
In the Junior Inter-County track and field match at Erith on August 16th, Peter Carton (4:29.2) and John Stow (4:36.0) finished 2nd and 5th respectively in the mile for Surrey.
John Stow produced his usual gutty run to cut our deficit to 39 seconds but Peter Carton was left to chase an invincible Ford (W.Surrey) who disappeared to set a new lap record (9:17).

Vic Butcher did not produce one of his best runs in finishing 10th on the first stage but Bill Curtin, Peter Carton and John Stow all put in useful sub-12 efforts to gain us deserved third place medals.
With two of our best runners unvailable---Peter Carton (competing for school) and John Stow (sick), and Bill Curtin below form we had no chance at all.

Peter's efforts have induced others to follow suit and climb to the standards set by Bill Curtin, so instead of having a solitary spearhead and a group of supporting runners down the field we now have Curtin, Carton and John Stow with little separating them and Tony Binda and Les Harris determined to close that gap.
He was fast catching John Stow who had put in some very hard work in the middle stages and was hanging on to his forward position with great determination.

With the terrible twins getting well clear early on, John Stow and Richard Langley gradually consolidated third and fourth places. Peter's two rivals, John Stow and Bill Curtin steered clear and pooled their resources in the 3,000 metres, Tony Binda also toned up. John found himself up against his Surrey County victor Ford(Aldershot F.D.) and Julian Goater (Shaftesbury) who is coached by the man who took Dave Bedford through to the Senior ranks.
The 'terrible triplets' (Peter Carton, Bill Curtin, John Stow) were on view in the 1500, which became a Belgrave v Aldershot F.D. match with Adams and Ford in the line-up.
There were many interesting contests during the afternoon but excitement built up for the clash between Bill Curtin, Peter Carton and John Stowe in the Junior 800 and 1500 events.
Peter Carton has the distinction of filling 11th place in the 800m., and 18th in the 5,000m., while John Stow shows up in 17th place over 3,000m.
John Stow remains to some extent the team's "dark horse". Beset by injury problems (fortunately not too serious), he has revealed little of his true potential yet.
John Stow looks comfortable as he dogs the footsteps of two brilliant juniors, Goater of Shaftesbury (10) and Ford of Aldershot (9) in the Southern junior 3,000m. - Photo: Ron Linstead
Tony Binda came 50th, John Stow 175th and Pat Breslin 197th The whole team except Mark appeared jaded - Bill although physically below par lacked nothing in determination - to beat Peter.
John Stow also won his County colours, but was going through a rough patch when this race came round, and finished 99th in 21m. 11s., nothing like the performance we know he can produce.

John Stow showed that he was recovering the form that makes him one of our brightest junior stars, with a good clocking on the first stage for the "A" team, and it was nice to see Derek Crooks turning out for us again.

Trevor Hart showed some improved form, in third place, while youths Bill Curtin, Peter Carton, Tony Binda and John Stow added to their growing reputations with fourth, sixth, seventh and twelfth, respectively.

Others aiming to get into the team will be PETER CARTON, BILL CURTIN, JOHN STOW, JOHN BICOURT, LAURIE O'HARA and JIM RIMMER, who says he's fitter than ever("I'am doing my own training this year") and also ADRIAN MAJOR.
It was good to see Paddy Breslin back in action in the junior events, and to see John Stow back in winning form, while there was a promising junior steeplechase from Mark Clancy.
In the junior 1,500m., there was a nerve-tingling late challenge from John Stow - showing some of his old fire - before Bill Curtin added this title to the 3,000m. he had won earlier.

Although this event was open to runners up to the age of 20, we scored a fine win with an all youth quartet. John Stow took the first stage and handed over to Tony Binda in 4th place recording 9m 2s. Tony clocked 8m 44s to move into 2nd position.

Recording 18m.53secs., Peter had 29 secs in hand over Tony Binda, who in turn was 17 secs up on Bill Curtin. John Stow, rapidly coming back to form was sixth. With a low total of 11 points we were easy winners of the team event.
Tony Binda was second, half a minute in arrears, and third was John Stow. Mark Clancy filled fourth spot with injury plagued Pat Breslin in fifth position.
The club 5,000m championship gave Laurie O'Hara his double - 14m 32.2s saw him almost 8s clear of the second man Peter Carton with John Stow coming in third.

Willie Williams was a hat-trick man in the junior events, while old rivals and team-mates John Stow and Bill Curtin shared the 800m. and 1,500m. titles, with John taking the former, and Bill the latter.

Laurie O'Hara almost a veteran was a comfortable second, well ahead of John Stow(almost a senior) who is 20 years Laurie's junior. Peter Carton was below form and Charlie Walker lost his vets crown to two new recruits to the "aged" division, Brian Gorman and Clive Shippen.
Although John slipped two places, only 61 seconds covered the first five teams---and Hercules Wimbledon were just 15 seconds behind us. STAGE 8: J.

A solid performance by our junior team, of Peter Carton (4th), Tony Binda (12th), Bill Curtin (17th) and John Stow (32nd) gave them a praiseworthy third - not all that far behind the winners, Thames Valley.

In the junior race, our famous four were 11th, with Peter Carton, who just missed a junior international,vest getting good support for his 10th place from Tony Binda (58th), Bill Curtin (109th) and John Stow (111th), and Mark Clancy again poised to fill any breach that should appear.
Far right: John Stow found himself the only competitor for the Junior race so ran a couple of laps in the '10'. Bottom left: 'Aussie' Bob Smith, a first team regular.
What a pity that our once unbeatable team of Tony Binda, Bill Curtin and John Stow , backing up Peter if not battling with him for individual honours, has now disintegrated.

With Gerry North still suffering from tonsilitis, John Stow stuck in a train at Raynes Park and our veterans girding themselves for the following days National Veteran's race, our chances became even slimmer.

But the lad who showed the best natural flair, on the track at any rate, was John Stow. John has kept in shape regularly enough to find that a solid year's work could also get him up to his rightful place in the forward position.
Top left: John Stow, who finished 2nd in 4:00.6, leads the 1500m field at Oxford. The winner was John Bicourt in 4:00.5, here in 4th position.

His time proved to be the fastest of the day by any of our long stage runners. STAGE 2: John Stow 16:04 (3rd fastest). The first of the short stages saw John setting off with Davies (TVH) haring after him.

John Stow, recovering from tonsilitis, hardly treated stage six like a convalescent's outing for he took us up two places overtaking Bartlett of Birchfield and Collins of Hercules Wimbledon in the process.

Cover photo - John Stow, currently enjoying his best ever season on the track, on his way to a 1500m victory in the Southern League. Judging is Bill Lucas and calling the lap times is Gordon Doubleday.

After setting a target of around 3:52 for the season, John Stow is going to have to think again. On the Friday night he qualified in the 1500m with an excellent personal best of 3:51.1 and then improved again in the final to equal John Bicourt's best, thus continuing their keen rivalry.

John Stow shocked everyone, including himself, with a 51.7 circuit in the same race. No brilliant performances this day on the field although our 'heavy boys' put in some good all-round work and Steve White again picked up top points in the Long Jump.

An 800 metre/ 1500 metre double was scored by John Stow who was untroubled over either distance. John Martin, resplendent in brand new javelin boots, beat his best distance with the 'spear' and if we can keep him off the beer and encourage him to concentrate on this event he is going to throw further still.
The Belgrave trio of John Stow (27), Colin Pearson (24) and Tony Fairclough (18) plough their way through the Surrey County Cross County Championship and help take the team to 2nd place.
John Stow pleased himself and the selectors for the Southern Relay with a very fine run after his gradual return to form in the latter part of the cross country season.
The 800 metres gave us more points than of late with both our men ducking under two minutes for the first time this year and John Stow later followed this with an impressive win in the 1,500 metres.

Following a brisk, bunched first lap the race soon formed into a pattern of small groups: Black, O'Hara, Stow and Carton in the first group were leading a second of North, Pearson and Mann; while further back a grimacing Clive Shippen was giving his younger rivals Coy, Jardine and Maughan a hard time.

Unusual too to see the likes of Gerry North, John Stow and Trevor Hart spectating rather than racing. Our new President sent 34 starters on their way, and a mile later a rather leisurely-paced group of eight led the field.

The pack is now strung out over a good 1½ miles but tonight those at the back get another chance to catch up because John Stow has to be peeled off the side of a bus shelter after running into it at full speed.
John Stow proved to be in good form for the approaching road relays and track season when he won the Club 5¾ mile Road Race Championship for the first time.

John Stow, '5¾' Champion for 1975, started out for the Bels. and clocking our fastest time of the day over the long stage, handed over to Jim Rimmer in 14th position in the middle of a line of runners with less than half a minute covering them.
John Stow ran a tactically perfect race. Running in the bunch but moving out and up whenever the current leader looked like breaking away, he reached 1200m with a crowd still round him.

Highlights included 22.9 for Charlie Gillett and 23.1 for Jim Evans over 200m, 49.8/400 Steve White, sub-50 from Steve and Charlie in the 4x400, 14:35.0/5000 from John Stow, 13.21/TJ from Steve Crosbie, 3.35/PV from Reg Hopkins ................................
Bill Kerr improved our best to 4:31 on leg 50 and was almost immediately overtaken by John Stow who remained far and away our fastest until John Bicourt's 98th leg of 4:14.

John Stow gave us our fastest league 5,000m of the year but still had to give way to SLH's redoubtable pair Roberts and Gevers whilst his partner Simon Lloyd had to vault the railings and run in flats to avoid missing the start.
Outstanding sellers were John Dunsford and Dennis Jones who got rid of 200 books at the London Transport Sports Meeting, and John Stow's mother who sold 35 books.

At the War Memorial with half a mile to go John Stow tried to surge away into a decisive lead but was unable to bring it off. Pat O'Connor was still close on his tail as the final turn into Lauriston Road came up and the track man was forced to turn on another fierce burst to ensure his win was beyond doubt.

John Stow underlined the fact that he is the man of the moment by leading home the claret and gold vests in spite of the welcome presence of Dick Piotrowski and Bob Richardson.

The leader for the premier pack is John Stow, who was nurtured at the Belgrave Breast and is now honed to a dangerous sharpness. A Titan of awe inspiring potential and putting it back in as, fast pack, leader.
A commanding performance came from John Stow in the 1,500m where, out for John Thresher's record of 3:54.0, he ran a solo 3:55.5. Good running too from a speedy looking Stu' Barrett.
He could be the man to give John Stow some opposition from within the Club. Another to gain early success in Belgrave colours is Jamie Stevenson.

John Stow did everything right but for the second successive year trailed Thames Valley's Clive Thomas home, unable to match his finishing burst over the last 150 metres.

John Phelan ran the 5,000m in 14:45 and John Stow failed to get into the 1500m final as fastest loser by 1.5 seconds - he ran 3:55. Steve White, running now in Oxford's colours, finished 6th in a good 400m final with 48.96.

The loss of men to the two 'away fixtures' meant that John Stow, keeping well away from peak fitness at this early stage of the season, had an effortless win by over two minutes to take his score up to four consecutive wins around this course.

Even with the rival attraction of the nearby Wimbledon '10', there was still a good turn-out for our Yacht '3', Ron Langheim being first away and John Stow following him 5 minutes 40 seconds and 49 runners later.
John Stow's ten-miling debut proved to be a most exciting one as, well towards the front of a large field at Woking, he chased Bill Weller to the line.

John Stow, elated with his Woking '10' performance of two weeks previous, appeared to be all set for a hat-trick of '5¾' championship wins and five consecutive victories around this course all told - especially as he had recovered from the 'flu' which had kept him out of action at the 'National'.

John Stow and Pam were married in September with many Belgravians present. It seems confusion was caused by Gordon Biscoe handing out numbers and pins at the reception while Colin Pearson spent half the time looking for the changing rooms!
John Stow, in Surrey's side for the SCAAA v Surrey v Wales v Police match on May 29th was unplaced in the 1500m. but nevertheless clocked 3:56.0 - a promising early season time.
Several old faces made a welcome re-appearance and rumour has it that old 'TK' will be battling it out with Tony Fairclough this winter. John Stow made a welcome return to clock fastest of the day

Ian Duncan ran a steady race to win from second claim member John Stow with the evergreen Laurie O'Hara yet again dipping under 30 minutes. The handicap was jointly won by the improving Youth John Gladwin and by Steve White, with Junior Mark Sinclair showing very good form to gain 3rd place.

And finally mention of Paul Richley's new Junior record of 8.33.7. The quality of this may be judged by reference to previous holders which have included ;Peter Carton,John Stow.Dave North, and Stu Paton!!!

In the mid 70's, John Stow ran up a record four consecutive wins with Oliver Foote taking three on the trot in 82/83; but very few Bels of the 80's have intervened at the sharp end of the list, only John Wright having made the top ten with an impressive solo 27.44 last March.
